explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/816: must a graph with 2n+1 vertices and n²+n+1 edges contain two equal-degree vertices joined by a path of length 3? Answered yes (Chen–Ma). The statement asserts this for all n ≥ 2; n = 1 is excluded as a genuine exception (the triangle). A Lean proof covering all n ≥ 2 is linked. HasEqualDegreePathThree uses a path (no repeated vertices) of length 3 between distinct u, v. Faithful.
